You're creating a portrait-format social media poster that showcases the 20 fastest-rising open-source coding AI repositories on GitHub for the week of April 9–15, 2026. Keep decorative elements minimal — let the data breathe. Star icons (⭐) or subtle GitHub-style iconography can reinforce the theme without cluttering.

This is **VERY IMPORTANT**: The reference must be refined so it enhances the work's depth without announcing itself. Think like a jazz musician quoting another song - only those who know will catch it, but everyone appreciates the music.

Anchor the piece with simple phrase(s) or details positioned subtly, using a limited color palette that feels intentional and cohesive. A punk venue poster might have larger, more aggressive type than a minimalist ceramics studio identity. Most of the time, font should be thin. All use of fonts must be design-forward and prioritize visual communication. Regardless of text scale, nothing falls off the page and nothing overlaps. This is non-negotiable for professional execution. **IMPORTANT: Use different fonts if writing text. Search the `./canvas-fonts` directory. Regardless of approach, sophistication is non-negotiable.**

Download and use whatever fonts are needed to make this a reality. Get creative by making the typography actually part of the art itself -- if the art is abstract, bring the font onto the canvas, not typeset digitally.

To push boundaries, follow design instinct/intuition while using the philosophy as a guiding principle. Embrace ultimate design freedom and choice. Push aesthetics and design to the frontier.

Make it appear as though someone at the absolute top of their field labored over every detail with painstaking care. Ensure the composition, spacing, color choices, typography - everything screams expert-level craftsmanship. Double-check that nothing overlaps, formatting is flawless, every detail perfect. Create something that could be shown to people to prove expertise and rank as undeniably impressive.

Output the final result as a single, downloadable .pdf or .png file, alongside the design philosophy used as a .md file.

Rather than adding a fun filter or refactoring a font, consider how to make the existing composition more cohesive with the art. If the instinct is to call a new function or draw a new shape, STOP and instead ask: "How can I make what's already here more of a piece of art?"

Take a second pass. Go back to the code and refine/polish further to make this a philosophically designed masterpiece.

To create additional pages when requested, create more creative pages along the same lines as the design philosophy but distinctly different as well. Bundle those pages in the same .pdf or many .pngs. Treat the first page as just a single page in a whole coffee table book waiting to be filled. arguments.content:
# Terminal Bloom

## Design Philosophy

**Terminal Bloom** is a visual language that treats data as spectacle — where raw numbers emerge from darkness like phosphorescent signals on a terminal screen, commanding attention through contrast and precision. The philosophy marries the austere authority of financial data terminals with the electric energy of open-source culture, creating artifacts that feel both rigorously systematic and vibrantly alive. Every element is meticulously crafted to appear as though countless hours were invested in its placement — the work of a master typographer and data designer laboring at the intersection of information and art.

**Space breathes through structured restraint.** Vast dark expanses are not emptiness but deliberate negative space — breathing room that lets data crystallize into meaning. The composition follows a vertical logic: metrics cascade downward like drops of light on a terminal screen, each one carrying weight. Visual hierarchy is established through scale, color temperature, and spatial density rather than decoration. Information flows from macro (headline numbers) to micro (full ranking table) with the authority of a well-designed annual report — authoritative, scannable, complete.

**Color is a data dimension, not decoration.** Electric blue (#00D4FF) marks rankings and structural elements — the spine of the visual system. Emerald green (#00FF88) signals positive momentum, upward trends, and growth. Warm amber (#FFB800) creates tension and attention — the color of new entries, anomalies, and the week's dominant story. Against the near-black canvas (#0A0A0F), these chromatic signals create an instant visual grammar: where you look first, what moves up, what's new. This is painstakingly calibrated chromatic design, the result of deep expertise in how color communicates at a glance.

**Typography is precise geometry with human warmth.** Numbers live in monospace — JetBrains Mono throughout — creating a systematic, scannable rhythm. Headlines use a bold geometric sans (Bricolage Grotesque) for authority without coldness. Labels are thin and restrained (Jura Light), whisper-quiet against the dark field. Every size, weight, and spacing decision has been refined through countless iterations to achieve visual balance — the product of master-level typographic craft. The hierarchy is absolute: rankings glow with importance, numbers breathe with legible spacing, context appears only to serve comprehension.

**Form follows function in systematic arrangement.** The poster functions as a single visual instrument, its architecture derived from the data itself. The full Top 20 ranking occupies the central real estate — each row a horizontal bar of information, rank numbers prominent, repo names scannable, star counts instantly legible. Thematic clusters are color-coded with chromatic tags that create instant pattern recognition without requiring reading. The dominant story (hermes-agent's +9,715) commands the visual mass of a headline, while supporting metrics float above as bold stat callouts. Decorative elements are forbidden — every shape exists to communicate, every color codes meaning, every pixel earns its place through labor-intensive refinement.

**The invisible hand of craft.** The philosophy demands that what appears effortless is actually the product of deep expertise — painstaking attention to kerning, multiple rounds of chromatic refinement, spatial relationships adjusted by fractions to achieve visual equilibrium. The result should feel like a Bloomberg terminal redesigned by a Bauhaus master: systematic rigor meets kinetic energy. Information architecture becomes art when executed at this level of obsessive precision — where the viewer senses not effort but inevitability, as though the design could not have been any other way.

        tag_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0] + 24

        tag_x += tag_w + 12

    table_y = 550

    draw.text((40, table_y), section_label2, font=font_label, fill=GRAY_MID)

    header_y = table_y + 30
    draw_gradient_bar(draw, 40, header_y, WIDTH - 80, 1, GRAY_DARK, GRAY_DARK)

    # Column headers
    draw.text((40, header_y + 12), "RNK", font=font_tag, fill=GRAY_MID)
    draw.text((90, header_y + 12), "REPOSITORY", font=font_tag, fill=GRAY_MID)
    draw.text((580, header_y + 12), "STARS", font=font_tag, fill=GRAY_MID)
    draw.text((720, header_y + 12), "CAT", font=font_tag, fill=GRAY_MID)

    repos = [
        (1, "NousResearch/hermes-agent", "+9,715", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (2, "forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills", "+4,917", "AI Util", ELECTRIC_BLUE),

        draw.line([(WIDTH - i - 1, 0), (WIDTH - i - 1, HEIGHT)], fill=(10, 10, 15, alpha), width=1)

    print("Poster saved to /app/output/final_poster.png")

    print(f"Dimensions: {img.size}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Coding AI Leaderboard Poster - Terminal Bloom Design Philosophy
Refined masterpiece with meticulous craftsmanship
"""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont, ImageFilter, ImageEnhance
import math

# Canvas dimensions (portrait)
WIDTH = 1080
HEIGHT = 1920

# Color palette - Terminal Bloom
BG_DARK = (10, 10, 15)
BG_CARD = (18, 18, 25)
ELECTRIC_BLUE = (0, 212, 255)
EMERALD_GREEN = (0, 255, 136)
AMBER = (255, 184, 0)
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
GRAY_LIGHT = (180, 180, 195)
GRAY_MID = (100, 100, 115)
GRAY_DARK = (50, 50, 60)
TEXT_DIM = (130, 135, 150)
CLAUDE_PURPLE = (167, 139, 250)

# Font paths
FONT_JETBRAINS_BOLD = "/logs/agent/sessions/skills/canvas-design/canvas-fonts/JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf"
FONT_JETBRAINS_REG = "/logs/agent/sessions/skills/canvas-design/canvas-fonts/JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf"
FONT_BRICOLAGE_BOLD = "/logs/agent/sessions/skills/canvas-design/canvas-fonts/BricolageGrotesque-Bold.ttf"
FONT_BRICOLAGE_REG = "/logs/agent/sessions/skills/canvas-design/canvas-fonts/BricolageGrotesque-Regular.ttf"
FONT_JURA_LIGHT = "/logs/agent/sessions/skills/canvas-design/canvas-fonts/Jura-Light.ttf"
FONT_JURA_MED = "/logs/agent/sessions/skills/canvas-design/canvas-fonts/Jura-Medium.ttf"

def load_font(path, size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype(path, size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.load_default()

def draw_glow_line(draw, x1, y1, x2, y2, color, width=1, glow_radius=8):
    """Draw a line with subtle glow effect"""
    for i in range(glow_radius):
        alpha = int(30 * (1 - i / glow_radius))
        r = int(color[0] + (BG_DARK[0] - color[0]) * (1 - alpha/30))
        g = int(color[1] + (BG_DARK[1] - color[1]) * (1 - alpha/30))
        b = int(color[2] + (BG_DARK[2] - color[2]) * (1 - alpha/30))
        draw.line([(x1, y1), (x2, y2)], fill=(r, g, b), width=width + i * 2)
    draw.line([(x1, y1), (x2, y2)], fill=color, width=width)

def create_poster():
    img = Image.new('RGB', (WIDTH, HEIGHT), BG_DARK)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

    # Load fonts
    font_h1 = load_font(FONT_BRICOLAGE_BOLD, 64)
    font_h2 = load_font(FONT_BRICOLAGE_BOLD, 44)
    font_h3 = load_font(FONT_BRICOLAGE_BOLD, 32)
    font_metric_value = load_font(FONT_JETBRAINS_BOLD, 52)
    font_metric_label = load_font(FONT_JURA_MED, 17)
    font_table_rank = load_font(FONT_JETBRAINS_BOLD, 20)
    font_table_name = load_font(FONT_BRICOLAGE_REG, 19)
    font_table_stars = load_font(FONT_JETBRAINS_BOLD, 19)
    font_table_trend = load_font(FONT_JETBRAINS_REG, 15)
    font_label = load_font(FONT_JURA_LIGHT, 15)
    font_tag = load_font(FONT_JURA_MED, 13)
    font_small = load_font(FONT_JURA_LIGHT, 12)
    font_takeaway = load_font(FONT_BRICOLAGE_REG, 17)

    # === HEADER SECTION ===
    # Top gradient accent line with glow
    for i in range(6):
        alpha = 80 - i * 12
        draw.line([(0, i), (WIDTH, i)], fill=(0, 180 + i*5, 220, 0), width=1)

    # Title
    title = "CODING AI LEADERBOARD"
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), title, font=font_h1)
    title_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    draw.text(((WIDTH - title_w) // 2, 40), title, font=font_h1, fill=WHITE)

    # Subtitle
    subtitle = "Top Open-Source GitHub Repos by Weekly Star Growth"
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), subtitle, font=font_label)
    sub_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    draw.text(((WIDTH - sub_w) // 2, 108), subtitle, font=font_label, fill=TEXT_DIM)

    # Date badge
    date_str = "◆ WEEK OF APR 9–15, 2026 ◆"
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), date_str, font=font_tag)
    date_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    draw.text(((WIDTH - date_w) // 2, 140), date_str, font=font_tag, fill=ELECTRIC_BLUE)

    # === HERMES-AGENT DOMINANT STORY ===
    hermes_y = 185
    # Vertical accent bar with glow
    draw_glow_line(draw, 45, hermes_y, 45, hermes_y + 120, AMBER, width=3, glow_radius=6)

    hermes_label = "★  WEEK'S BIGGEST STORY"
    draw.text((62, hermes_y + 2), hermes_label, font=font_label, fill=AMBER)

    hermes_name = "hermes-agent"
    draw.text((62, hermes_y + 28), hermes_name, font=font_h2, fill=WHITE)

    # Hero stars with emphasis
    hermes_stars = "+9,715"
    draw.text((62, hermes_y + 78), hermes_stars, font=font_metric_value, fill=AMBER)

    hermes_context = "stars  ·  NousResearch"
    draw.text((62 + 200, hermes_y + 88), hermes_context, font=font_small, fill=TEXT_DIM)

    # === METRICS ROW ===
    metrics_y = 340
    metrics = [
        ("~48K", "Total Stars Across Top 20"),
        ("10", "Repos Gained 2k+ Stars"),
        ("5", "Claude-Related Repos"),
    ]

    metric_colors = [ELECTRIC_BLUE, EMERALD_GREEN, CLAUDE_PURPLE]
    spacing = WIDTH // 3

    for i, ((value, label), color) in enumerate(zip(metrics, metric_colors)):
        x = 45 + i * spacing

        # Subtle vertical divider
        if i > 0:
            draw.line([(x - 5, metrics_y + 5), (x - 5, metrics_y + 100)],
                      fill=GRAY_DARK, width=1)

        # Accent dot
        draw.ellipse([x, metrics_y + 8, x + 8, metrics_y + 16], fill=color)

        # Value
        draw.text((x + 16, metrics_y), value, font=font_metric_value, fill=color)

        # Label (split into two lines if needed)
        label_lines = label.split(' ')
        if len(label_lines) > 1:
            draw.text((x + 16, metrics_y + 62), ' '.join(label_lines[:-1]),
                     font=font_small, fill=TEXT_DIM)
            draw.text((x + 16, metrics_y + 78), label_lines[-1],
                     font=font_small, fill=TEXT_DIM)
        else:
            draw.text((x + 16, metrics_y + 65), label, font=font_small, fill=TEXT_DIM)

    # === SECTION DIVIDER ===
    section_y = 470
    draw.line([(40, section_y), (WIDTH - 40, section_y)], fill=GRAY_DARK, width=1)

    # === EMERGING THEMES ===
    themes_y = section_y + 25

    section_label = "EMERGING THEMES"
    draw.text((40, themes_y), section_label, font=font_label, fill=GRAY_MID)

    # Theme tags in a refined layout
    themes = [
        ("Agent Frameworks", EMERALD_GREEN),
        ("Claude Code Ecosystem", CLAUDE_PURPLE),
        ("AI Utilities", ELECTRIC_BLUE),
        ("Design Tools", AMBER),
    ]

    tag_x = 40
    tag_y = themes_y + 28
    max_y = tag_y + 40

    for theme, color in themes:
        bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), theme, font=font_tag)
        tag_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0] + 28
        tag_h = 36

        # Tag background with subtle fill
        fill_color = (color[0] // 18, color[1] // 18, color[2] // 18)
        draw.rounded_rectangle((tag_x, tag_y, tag_x + tag_w, tag_y + tag_h),
                               radius=6, fill=fill_color)
        draw.rounded_rectangle((tag_x, tag_y, tag_x + tag_w, tag_y + tag_h),
                               radius=6, outline=color, width=1)

        # Tag text
        draw.text((tag_x + 14, tag_y + 10), theme, font=font_tag, fill=color)

        tag_x += tag_w + 14

    # === FULL RANKING TABLE ===
    table_y = max_y + 35

    section_label2 = "FULL TOP 20 RANKING"
    draw.text((40, table_y), section_label2, font=font_label, fill=GRAY_MID)

    # Table header background
    header_y = table_y + 28
    draw.rectangle([40, header_y, WIDTH - 40, header_y + 40], fill=(16, 16, 24))

    # Column headers
    draw.text((48, header_y + 12), "RANK", font=font_tag, fill=GRAY_MID)
    draw.text((100, header_y + 12), "REPOSITORY", font=font_tag, fill=GRAY_MID)
    draw.text((570, header_y + 12), "STARS", font=font_tag, fill=GRAY_MID)
    draw.text((700, header_y + 12), "TYPE", font=font_tag, fill=GRAY_MID)

    # Table header bottom border
    draw.line([(40, header_y + 40), (WIDTH - 40, header_y + 40)], fill=GRAY_DARK, width=1)

    # Ranking data
    repos = [
        (1, "NousResearch/hermes-agent", "+9,715", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (2, "forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills", "+4,917", "AI Util", ELECTRIC_BLUE),
        (3, "JuliusBrussee/caveman", "+4,407", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (4, "MemPalace/mempalace", "+3,524", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (5, "VoltAgent/awesome-design-md", "+3,246", "Design", AMBER),
        (6, "microsoft/markitdown", "+3,048", "AI Util", ELECTRIC_BLUE),
        (7, "safishamsi/graphify", "+2,763", "Design", AMBER),
        (8, "obra/superpowers", "+2,180", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (9, "shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice", "+2,151", "Claude", CLAUDE_PURPLE),
        (10, "affaan-m/everything-claude-code", "+1,978", "Claude", CLAUDE_PURPLE),
        (11, "thedotmack/claude-mem", "+1,828", "Claude", CLAUDE_PURPLE),
        (12, "santifer/career-ops", "+1,788", "AI Util", ELECTRIC_BLUE),
        (13, "multica-ai/multica", "+1,506", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (14, "shiyu-coder/Kronos", "+1,286", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (15, "ultraworkers/claw-code", "+1,285", "Claude", CLAUDE_PURPLE),
        (16, "openclaw/openclaw", "+1,268", "Claude", CLAUDE_PURPLE),
        (17, "OpenBMB/VoxCPM", "+1,266", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (18, "addyosmani/agent-skills", "+1,195", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
        (19, "rtk-ai/rtk", "+1,098", "AI Util", ELECTRIC_BLUE),
        (20, "garrytan/gstack", "+1,012", "Agent", EMERALD_GREEN),
    ]

    row_h = 40
    row_start_y = header_y + 50

    for i, (rank, name, stars, cat, cat_color) in enumerate(repos):
        row_y = row_start_y + i * row_h

        # Alternating subtle background for readability
        if i % 2 == 0:
            draw.rectangle([40, row_y, WIDTH - 40, row_y + row_h - 1],
                          fill=(14, 14, 20))

        # Left accent for top 5
        if rank <= 5:
            draw.line([(40, row_y), (40, row_y + row_h - 1)],
                      fill=ELECTRIC_BLUE, width=2)

        # Rank number - monospace precision
        rank_str = f"{rank:2d}"
        rank_color = ELECTRIC_BLUE if rank <= 3 else GRAY_LIGHT
        draw.text((48, row_y + 9), rank_str, font=font_table_rank, fill=rank_color)

        # Repository name
        max_chars = 32
        display_name = name if len(name) <= max_chars else name[:max_chars - 2] + "…"
        draw.text((100, row_y + 10), display_name, font=font_table_name, fill=WHITE)

        # Stars with color coding
        stars_color = AMBER if rank == 1 else (GRAY_LIGHT if rank <= 10 else GRAY_MID)
        draw.text((570, row_y + 10), stars, font=font_table_stars, fill=stars_color)

        # Category tag - compact pill
        cat_bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), cat, font=font_tag)
        cat_w = cat_bbox[2] - cat_bbox[0] + 16
        cat_x = 700
        draw.rounded_rectangle((cat_x, row_y + 7, cat_x + cat_w, row_y + 29),
                               radius=4, fill=(cat_color[0]//22, cat_color[1]//22, cat_color[2]//22))
        draw.text((cat_x + 8, row_y + 9), cat, font=font_tag, fill=cat_color)

    # Bottom table border
    table_bottom_y = row_start_y + 20 * row_h + 5
    draw.line([(40, table_bottom_y), (WIDTH - 40, table_bottom_y)], fill=GRAY_DARK, width=1)

    # === KEY TAKEAWAYS ===
    takeaways_y = table_bottom_y + 35

    draw.text((40, takeaways_y), "KEY TAKEAWAYS", font=font_label, fill=GRAY_MID)

    takeaways = [
        "Agent-first development is surging — hermes-agent's +9,715 stars dwarf every other entry",
        "Claude Code ecosystem expanding fast — 25% of the top 20 orbit a single product",
        "Utility tools like markitdown show foundational packages sustain interest alongside agent projects",
    ]

    for j, takeaway in enumerate(takeaways):
        ty = takeaways_y + 30 + j * 36

        # Refined bullet
        draw.ellipse([44, ty + 7, 50, ty + 13], fill=ELECTRIC_BLUE)

        # Text with proper spacing
        draw.text((60, ty + 2), takeaway, font=font_takeaway, fill=GRAY_LIGHT)

    # === FOOTER ===
    footer_y = HEIGHT - 65

    # Footer divider with gradient effect
    for i in range(2):
        draw.line([(40, footer_y + i), (WIDTH - 40, footer_y + i)], fill=GRAY_DARK, width=1)

    # Data source - centered
    source_text = "Data: star-history.com  ·  Week of April 9–15, 2026"
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), source_text, font=font_small)
    source_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    draw.text(((WIDTH - source_w) // 2, footer_y + 18), source_text, font=font_small, fill=GRAY_MID)

    # Bottom accent line with electric gradient
    for i in range(4):
        ratio = i / 4
        r = int(ELECTRIC_BLUE[0] * (1 - ratio) + AMBER[0] * ratio)
        g = int(ELECTRIC_BLUE[1] * (1 - ratio) + AMBER[1] * ratio)
        b = int(ELECTRIC_BLUE[2] * (1 - ratio) + AMBER[2] * ratio)
        draw.line([(0, HEIGHT - 4 + i), (WIDTH, HEIGHT - 4 + i)], fill=(r, g, b), width=1)

    # === EDGE VIGNETTE ===
    # Subtle darkening at edges for depth
    edge_width = 25
    for i in range(edge_width):
        alpha = int(20 * (1 - i / edge_width))
        # Left edge
        draw.line([(i, 0), (i, HEIGHT)], fill=(5, 5, 10), width=1)
        # Right edge
        draw.line([(WIDTH - i - 1, 0), (WIDTH - i - 1, HEIGHT)], fill=(5, 5, 10), width=1)

    # Apply subtle sharpening
    enhancer = ImageEnhance.Sharpness(img)
    img = enhancer.enhance(1.1)

    # Save
    img.save("/app/output/final_poster.png", "PNG", quality=95)
    print("Refined poster saved to /app/output/final_poster.png")
    print(f"Dimensions: {img.size}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
